- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to prevent over-optimism.
- In low-sentiment periods with mean-reverting history, model often fails to recognize reversion; adjust forecast toward 30-day moving average or 10-day weighted average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to ignore it; add 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid lagged overconfidence.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher sentiment → less smoothing, lower sentiment → more smoothing.
